line: But I know better Than to drive you home ’Cause you’d invite me in And I’d be yours again
meaning: Billie is trying to go solo and make her own path, and she knows that she’ll wanna be back with her ex if they invite her in.

line: I’d (I’d) like to be your answer (Be your answer) ’Cause you’re so handsome (You’re so handsome)
vault_lines: I'd (I'd) like to be your answer (Be your answer)
meaning: Billie is trying to resist the urge of going back to her ex.

line: Can’t you hear me? I’m not comin’ home Do you understand? I’ve changed my plans
meaning: Billie’s lover or family doesn’t want to accept the fact that she’s leaving for good. It could be a breakup and she’s trying to find herself again, or just her wanting to change.

line: I can’t seem to focus And you don’t seem to notice I’m not here I’m just a mirror You check your complexion To find your reflection’s all alone I had to go
meaning:
Billie’s headspace in the intro to my future is melancholic; her head is filled and her partner isn’t responding in the way she desires in relationships. Whether or not he is blatantly ignoring her or engaging incorrectly, he isn’t giving her the connection she’s looking for. In her sixth Vanity Fair interview Billie shares the importance of touch in her relationships, so perhaps the physical aspect is what’s missing in this relationship.

By saying she’s “just a mirror” Billie is inputting the idea that she is putting on (reflecting) the person that her partner wants instead of who she really is inside. In idontwannabeyouanymore, Billie personifies a mirror with the image of a pure representation of yourself which is taken in a negative way. So when he looks to see Billie, he sees an unfamiliar personality. This line can also be taken in a literal sense, in which she literally abandons him, in a harsh, yet necessary way.

This intro verse is a version of karma in a melancholic form taken by Billie.

line: I know supposedly I’m lonely now (Lonely now) Know I’m supposed to be unhappy Without someone (Someone) But aren’t I someone? (Aren’t I someone? Yeah)
vault_lines: I know supposedly I'm lonely now (Lonely now)
meaning:
In an interview with Zane Lowe, Billie spoke about her loneliness and eventual growth:

I spent years and years relying on someone and as soon as I didn’t have a someone, I got somebody else. And I’m not talking about relationships, I’m talking about everything. I could never be alone. I couldn’t take my own company. I just felt like I needed that growth. I needed a moment to myself and I got it. It was hard, it’s so much harder than you think to not rely on people, to just have yourself to rely on. It’s weird, it’s not something you’d think about being hard but when you’re in that “alone zone” it’s a new feeling. I really wanted to talk about it. Everything is about love. There’s nothing that talks about being alone is really powerful and you grow a lot and you learn a lot and it’s not bad.

Billie struggled with severe separation anxiety during her childhood to the point that one of her parents constantly had to be around her. In an interview with Rolling Stone, Billie’s parents explained that because of her separation anxiety, she slept with her parents until she was 10 or 12.

line: ’Cause I, I’m in love With my future Can’t wait to meet her And I (I), I’m in love But not with anybody else Just wanna get to know myself
meaning:
In the chorus, Billie sings about her enthusiasm for the future and what it has in store for her. Billie explained further in an email sent to fans:

when we wrote this song, it was exactly where my head was at – hopeful, excited and a craaaazy amount of self reflection and self growth. but recently it has also taken on a lot of new meaning in the context of what’s happening in the world now

The COVID-19 pandemic, also known as the coronavirus pandemic, has impacted countless lives worldwide and caused uncertainty for the future. Billie acknowledges these fears, but she instead chooses to have a more optimistic view of the future. In the email she sent to her fans after the release of “my future,” Billie spoke about maintaining her optimism:

the future feels uncertain and crazy right now. but i think we need to be ready to put the work in, and if we do that, we should be hopeful and excited for our future. i have to keep reminding myself that the future is ours, and i know we want to do everything we can to make it better for everyone in the world. and for the world itself… it’s up to us to change things now. not only for us, but for future generations. stay hopeful.

In a July 2020 interview with Zane Lowe, Billie explained the final line of the song:

There’s still hope in it. We will get out of this eventually. It might take years, but we’ll be okay eventually.
